license_status.assessment: Conflicting repository text; commercial reuse not treated as clarified

principal_findings: Review path compares one bid response or that response's technical/business split against requirements
No multi-bidder ranking or weighted procurement scoring engine evidenced in reviewed schema and routes
Bidding path manages parameter catalogs and exports a two-column Word technical parameter name table
Review headline uses satisfied-item percentage with an 80-percent threshold; no mandatory-veto branch in that logic
Format score is model output based on extracted text, not rendered-page or font-metric validation
Three analysis calls are sequential in current app.py despite parallel wording in documents
Model inputs are truncated to fixed character limits without a corresponding full-scope coverage manifest
Input text and results are stored in SQLite and sent in model requests; local parsing does not establish local inference
No user/organization ownership model or per-item human adjudication trail evidenced in reviewed application code
Global recent-three-job trimming is unsuitable as a project archive policy without further design
design_implications: Separate procurement authoring, bidder authoring and assisted evaluation roles
Freeze requirement and scoring rule versions before evaluation
Judge mandatory requirements before ordinary coverage percentages
Preserve source locators, extraction completeness and explicit partial-result status
Record actual human review and keep supplier evidence isolated
